name: Salt glazing
summary: Rock salt is thrown into a kiln at stoneware heat. The salt vapour reacts with the clay and forms a thin hard glaze with an orange-peel texture.
how: Throw 1 to 2 kg of rock salt for each cubic metre through ports in the kiln wall.
Seal the ports and let the vapour settle for 20 to 30 minutes.
Keep the wall 4 mm or more thick, so that the pot does not crack in the heat shock.

origin.note: Potters of Siegburg and Raeren glaze stoneware with salt in the 15th century.

adoptions.via: Rhineland potters glaze jugs and jars with salt from about 1400, so that the pots hold liquids without a lead lining.
American potters throw salt in the kiln to glaze crocks and jugs, with the same method that the Rhenish potters use.
